findings.title: GitHub installer validation is skipped when Integration row does not exist yet
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the first `except Integration.DoesNotExist` immediately returns `pipeline.next_step()`. This means if the GitHub installation webhook has not yet created the `Integration` row when the browser completes the Sentry setup pipeline (or if it never does), the sender check is bypassed completely. The pipeline then proceeds to `build_integration`, which uses the app JWT to fetch the installation by user-supplied `installation_id` and creates the Integration without `metadata.sender`. An attacker with a Sentry session and a known/guessed `installation_id` can therefore link a GitHub installation to their Sentry organization without being the GitHub user who installed it. The check should fail closed in this path, or `build_integration` should require/derive and store the installer and validate it.

findings.title: Direct metadata indexing can raise KeyError for integrations without sender
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every active Integration has a `sender` dict with `login`. However `build_integration` only sets `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, and the pipeline state does not populate `sender`, so integrations created through this fallback (and older rows) may lack it. When this branch is reached for such an Integration, the request raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the intended installation error page. Use `.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and handle a missing value explicitly.
